items.followUp: What is video conferencing used for?

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying that video conferencing allows live audio and video communication.
rubric.description: States that communication takes place in real time using audio and video.
rubric.how: Check that the answer identifies live audio-and-video communication; equivalent wording is acceptable.

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying communication over a network between people in different places.
rubric.description: Mentions communication over a network or between people in different locations.
rubric.how: Accept either a network connection or communication between geographically separate participants.

modelAnswer: Video conferencing is real-time communication between people in different locations using audio and video over a network.
It allows participants to see and talk to one another, usually through the Internet.

items.followUp: Write any two advantages of Star Topology.

rubric.why: A valid advantage is that orderly transmission, often through token passing, helps prevent data collisions.
rubric.description: Gives a valid advantage related to orderly data transmission or avoiding collisions.
rubric.how: Award for a correct ring-topology advantage such as token passing preventing collisions.

rubric.why: A second distinct valid advantage is required.
rubric.description: Gives another valid advantage of ring topology.
rubric.how: Accept a distinct advantage, such as equal access, good performance under heavy traffic, or ease of locating a fault.

modelAnswer: Data travels in an orderly manner around the ring, which helps prevent collisions.
Each computer gets an opportunity to transmit data; the network can perform well under heavy traffic.

rubric.why: The defining role of the server is to provide services or resources.
rubric.description: Identifies a server that provides services or resources.
rubric.how: Award for stating the server's provider role.

rubric.why: The defining role of a client is to request or use what the server provides.
rubric.description: Identifies clients that request or use the server's services or resources.
rubric.how: Award for stating the client role; interpret the question as referring to a client-server network.

modelAnswer: A client-server network is a network in which one or more servers provide services or resources.
The client computers request and use the services or resources provided by the server.

items.followUp: What is an empty HTML tag? Give one example.

accept: does not need a closing tag
rubric.why: A singular tag is not paired with a separate closing tag.
rubric.description: States that a singular tag has no separate closing tag.
rubric.how: Award for a clear statement that the tag is not closed by a matching end tag.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates the definition.

modelAnswer: A singular tag is an HTML tag that does not need a separate closing tag.

items.followUp: Write any two attributes of the <a> tag.

rubric.why: One correct image-tag attribute earns one mark.
rubric.description: Names one valid attribute of the tag.
rubric.how: Accept src, alt, width, or height.

rubric.why: A second attribute must also be named.
rubric.description: Names a second valid attribute of the tag.
rubric.how: Award only when the student names two distinct valid attributes in total.

modelAnswer: Two attributes of the tag are src and alt.
The src attribute specifies the image file, and alt provides alternative text.

items.followUp: Which HTML entity is used to insert a non-breaking space?

rubric.why: The required HTML entity for a non-breaking space is  .
The answer should explain the purpose of the entity in webpage text.
rubric.description: Explains that the entity inserts a space in the text.
rubric.how: Accept that it inserts a non-breaking space or is used to add spaces.

modelAnswer: Use the HTML entity   to insert a non-breaking space in webpage text.
Repeat   when more than one such space is required.

items.followUp: Write the body tag code to set a green background and black text.

rubric.why: The body tag's bgcolor attribute sets the page background colour to blue.
rubric.description: Uses the body tag and sets its background colour to blue.
rubric.how: Award for a body element with bgcolor set to blue.

rubric.why: The body tag's text attribute sets the foreground text colour to red.
rubric.description: Sets the page's text colour to red.
rubric.how: Award for text set to red in the body tag.

items.followUp: Explain the purpose of the input/output and decision symbols in a flowchart.

rubric.why: The terminal symbol is used for the start or end of a flowchart.
rubric.description: Identifies the terminal symbol and its use.
rubric.how: Award for oval/ellipse and start or end.

rubric.why: A rectangle represents a processing step or instruction.
rubric.description: Identifies the process symbol and its use.
rubric.how: Award for rectangle and a processing operation.

rubric.why: A parallelogram represents data entering or leaving the process.
rubric.description: Identifies the input/output symbol and its use.
rubric.how: Award for parallelogram and input or output.

rubric.why: A diamond represents a condition whose result leads to alternative paths.
rubric.description: Identifies the decision symbol and branching on a condition.
rubric.how: Award for diamond and a decision/branch, commonly labelled Yes and No.

modelAnswer: Terminal (oval): shows the beginning or end of a flowchart.
Process (rectangle): shows an operation, instruction or calculation.
Input/Output (parallelogram): shows data being entered into or displayed by the system.
Decision (diamond): shows a condition and branches the flow, commonly into Yes and No paths.
